newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia says Gazprom has settled government debts.
newsitem.headline: Russia says Gazprom has settled government debts.

text.p: Russian natural gas producer Gazprom has settled all its debts to the government, First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov said on Sunday.
"Gazprom has completely paid off its debts to the budget," Nemtsov told Reuters. "It paid the last time on June 26 ...(it was) a lot of money -- over 10 trillion (roubles) ($1.74 billion)."

Gazprom chief executive Rem Vyakhirev said on Wednesday Gazprom had settled up completely with the government, paying more than 14.5 trillion roubles ($2.52 billion) in overdue tax payments, which he said could help pay state pensions.
Government spokesman Igor Shabdurasulov had said last week that Gazprom had settled accounts with the government although it still owed money to the state pension fund.
Gazprom finance director Mikahil Dokuchayev said later the company still owed 3.5 trillion roubles ($607 million) in taxes but had paid dues to the Pension fund.

Gazprom, under pressure from the government to settle up with overdue taxes and payments to state organs, was also racing to pay off debts as it prepared to raise capital abroad for its $45 billion Yamal-Europegas production and pipeline project.
Government and company officials had said the company would clear all its debt by the end of the month.

Tax collection has jumped to the top of the government's agenda in recent months. Tax revenues have been far below target for the first four months of the year and have forced it to battle with parliament over proposed deep budget cuts.
